title: fix(spec)!: engine-side searchFields declarations refuse an empty list, as FullTextSearchSchema.fields does
body:
domain:spec#1 · os-tesla · session_01L9qibwb6hBqszPTYJobitm

<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-tesla"} -->
_Requested by **Tesla** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao?thread=cmsg_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6JaoDByYUjCh5NqsyFHj21fAy6)_

Fixes #28059

Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：引擎侧三处 `searchFields` 声明（`EngineQueryOptionsSchema`、`EngineAggregateOptionsSchema`、`EngineCountOptionsSchema`）改用共享的搜索字段数组规则，空数组 `[]` 被拒收，并带上与 `QuerySchema.searchFields` 相同的说明文字。
- 为什么改：同一个 schema 上 `search: { fields: [] }` 已被拒收，`searchFields: []` 却被接受，而 Data API 入口和引擎（#27732 进行中）都拒收它；按发布的类型或 JSON Schema 写代码的嵌入方和 AI 会被误导。
- 风险与回滚：只收窄声明，TypeScript 类型不变（仍是 `string[] | undefined`）；引擎运行时不用这三个 schema 解析选项，所以直接调用引擎的行为本 PR 不变。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/spec/src/data/data-engine.zod.ts`（三处声明）、`packages/spec/src/data/search-fields-names-a-field.test.ts`（原「仍接受空数组」的阶段边界测试翻转为拒收测试）、`.changeset/28059-engine-search-fields-names-a-field.md`（BREAKING 说明与 ADR-0087 处置）。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run src/data/search-fields-names-a-field.test.ts`，预期全部通过，其中包括 “EngineQueryOptionsSchema.searchFields refuses an empty list with the accept-set sentence”。
- 需要你做的：无。席内契约复审 PASS（评论 6525975157），由席位落地。

## What changes

- `EngineQueryOptionsSchema.searchFields`, `EngineAggregateOptionsSchema.searchFields` and `EngineCountOptionsSchema.searchFields` change from `z.array(z.string()).optional()` to `searchFieldsArray().optional()`, the array arm `QuerySchema.searchFields` and `FullTextSearchSchema.fields` already use (`./search-fields-names-a-field.ts`, imported by this file already). An empty list is refused at `searchFields` with the shared sentence. A list with a blank member is still admitted, as the shared arm admits it. One accept set, no fresh `.min(1)`.
- Each of the three now carries a `.describe()` ending in the shared `SEARCH_FIELDS_ACCEPT_SET`, so the published JSON Schema and the reference docs state the rule. `content/docs/references/data/data-engine.mdx` is regenerated (3 lines).
- The module docblock of `search-fields-names-a-field.ts` drops "the engine-side declarations do not take it yet".
- Changeset `28059-engine-search-fields-names-a-field.md`: `@objectstack/spec` patch (`Metadata-protocol: none`), `fix(spec)!`, both declaration lines, ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, and a "Supersedes" note for the unreleased #27683 entry's bullet that said these declarations still admit `[]`.

**Engine behaviour on `main`.** The in-process engine does not parse its options with these schemas, but since #28108 (`6a648ac2`, #27732, merged before this PR and shipping in the same release) it refuses `searchFields: []` and `search.fields: []` itself with `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` before any driver read. This branch's merge base predates that commit, so on this branch's own tree the engine still reads `[]` as absent; after the merge the declaration, the Data API doors and the engine refuse the same value. (Seat correction: the earlier sentence said the engine refusal was still in flight.)

## Tests

`packages/spec/src/data/search-fields-names-a-field.test.ts`:

- The stage-boundary block "the engine-side searchFields declarations are the next stage" (which asserted `[]` is still admitted) is replaced by "the engine-side searchFields declarations":
  - `%s.searchFields refuses an empty list with the accept-set sentence`, for each of the three schemas: `success: false`, issue `path` equal to `['searchFields']`, message equal to `SEARCH_FIELDS_NAMES_NO_FIELD`.
  - `%s.searchFields answers [] as its structured search.fields does`: the bare and structured spellings on the same schema give the same message.
  - `keeps %s unchanged` (one name, two names, a blank member) and `still admits no searchFields at all`, for each schema.
- "the declarations state the accept set they enforce" gains the three engine members.

<details><summary>Ablation: removing the narrowing turns the new refusal cases red</summary>

On committed head `fca20448`, all three declarations were reverted to `z.array(z.string()).optional()` (3 anchors replaced, 0 fixed spellings left, counted with `grep -c`). `vitest run src/data/search-fields-names-a-field.test.ts`: 6 failed | 51 passed (57), exactly the 3 refusal and 3 same-answer cases. The file was restored with `git checkout HEAD --`, and `git diff HEAD` was empty. The describe-sentence cases stayed green because the mutation kept the `.describe()`.
</details>

## Acceptance notes

- The claim writes `Clause-②: no`. The order and triage `6522171038` write `no (narrowing)`, and this is a narrowing, so this body and the changeset carry `no (narrowing)`.
- A whitespace-only or blank member (`['']`) is still admitted by all three declarations, as by `QuerySchema.searchFields`. The doors refuse a blank member as an unknown field. This PR leaves that alone, as #27683 did.
- No in-repo caller parses an engine option bag holding `searchFields: []` with these schemas (`git grep` of `searchFields: []` outside the spec test: only door-level tests in rest and objectql, which go through `findData`, not these schemas).
